newsitem.title: UK: LME expects criticism to continue despite review.
newsitem.headline: LME expects criticism to continue despite review.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) expects criticism over its methods to continue, even though Thursday's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review approved its practices, LME Chief Executive David King said..

The review was commissioned by the LME after June's Sumitomo Corp scandal erupted. The Exchange came in for criticism over its unique trading practices and customs, such as non-cash clearing, from quarters such as the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), which also trades copper futures.

"NYMEX will continue to grumble...They continue to lose market share," King said. The SIB, Britain's top regulator, carried out a wholesale review of the LME after the Sumitomo scandal in mid-June, when the Japanese company fired its head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.

The review suggested some changes and increased transparancy, but came down on the side of retaining key elements such as non-cash clearing, inter-office and ring trading, and non-segregation of funds.
"Since the review soundly endorses the way we operate, there is little likelihood of NYMEX's prospects improving," King said.
